structure.title: Book One · The Ingmar farm
structure.text: A farmer tries to decide what is right by imagining how an ancestor would judge him. The opening gives the farm a voice in family decisions. In later disputes, selling a piece of land can feel like answering back to several generations of the dead.

structure.title: Book Two · The mission house
structure.text: A schoolmaster hopes to give religious enthusiasm a home in the village. A flood, a recovery and the arrival of a preacher alter whom people trust to speak for God. The same event acquires different meanings depending on which household tells it.

structure.title: Book Three · The decision to leave
structure.text: A story of disaster at sea draws the Swedish households into the orbit of believers abroad. In this volume the pilgrimage is felt chiefly in the village it will empty. Lovers, farms and family expectations must all find a price when departure becomes a practical undertaking.

people.name: Karin
people.text: Karin has obligations to a family name, an estate and the people who come to worship. When her religious allegiance changes, all three come with her into a decision someone less established could have made privately.

people.name: Hellgum
people.text: People attach enormous hopes to the signs surrounding Hellgum. His influence grows through the work of followers who must continue interpreting his wishes even when the preacher himself is elsewhere.

people.name: Young Ingmar and Gertrude
people.role: Heir to the farm and schoolmaster’s daughter
people.text: Their attachment might once have looked like a village matter for two families to settle. The sale of the farm and the prospect of emigration put a second question inside any promise they make. Where would they have to live in order to keep it?

context.title: Faith has a local economy
context.text: For people who live on family land, leaving for Jerusalem entails the sale of tools, furniture and farms. A neighbour who declines to share the revelation may nevertheless have to buy something, lose someone or watch a claim on an inheritance disappear.

notice.text: Listen for a change from one person's story to the village's version.
notice.why: A private experience can travel as rumour, warning or miracle. By the time it reaches another kitchen it may be evidence in a dispute the person concerned never intended to enter.

notice.text: Notice the onlookers at a sale or a departure.
notice.why: The spectacle brings believers and doubters into the same physical space. A familiar object crossing from one pair of hands to another can register what the prospect of the Holy Land means to the people staying behind.

passages.quote: there was an auction sale at the Ingmar Farm

opening: The farms in this Swedish valley carry generations of work, family pride, and promises about who will inherit. Then a religious awakening persuades some of their owners that God wants them somewhere else. Leaving for Jerusalem sounds like an act of faith until the land must be sold and the people staying behind discover what devotion will cost them. Lagerlöf makes the pull of the ancestral home powerful enough that the decision to abandon it cannot be understood simply as courage or delusion.
